primitives.name: Prepare-Not-Flip Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: # PROVE THE EDGE — One-Sitting Proof Chain > **Prepare-not-flip.** This runbook is the exact ordered command sequence that takes the owner > from empty tables to a published-ready calibration story in a single sitting.
primitives.assumptions: Owner controls execution flow; no agent intervention allowed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Execution order is deterministic and non-reversible once production steps begin.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic verification pipeline where each step must be reproducible before flipping to production state.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of ordered execution steps without data mutation.

primitives.name: Closing Line Value (CLV)
primitives.verbatim_quote: (Source: `docs/strategy/PATH_TO_PROVEN_EDGE.md`, Part I §3 / §4.) The real north star is **Closing Line Value (CLV)**: did we get a better number than the line closed at?
primitives.assumptions: Market closing line represents aggregated sharp betting intelligence; CLV measures deviation from that baseline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Only meaningful when compared against actual closing line and realized outcome.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's market calibration engine, used to compute expected value relative to closing odds.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative CLV score across 200+ settled bets.

primitives.name: Historical Settlement Backfill
primitives.verbatim_quote: > > The whole point of Phase 14 is to convert "trust us, we'll show results later" into > "here is 25 seasons of reliability curve, here is the code, reproduce it." The strongest trust > asset is a proof nobody can fake.
primitives.assumptions: Frozen model predictions are rerun on pre-game data to simulate historical performance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Requires full historical dataset and frozen model version to avoid contamination of live data.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSI's replay mechanism for validating model consistency over time using static inputs.
layer2.telemetry: Number of games settled with CLV and associated reliability metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality lies between trust and reproducibility: the system assumes that a model’s edge is only credible if it can be independently verified through a deterministic sequence of actions. The 'prepare-not-flip' protocol enforces this by separating read-only steps from write-only ones, ensuring no accidental mutation occurs during testing. The CLV primitive acts as a scalar measure of model superiority over the market, derived from comparing predicted probabilities against actual closing lines. Its reliability is anchored in the assumption that the closing line reflects true market consensus. The backfill process ensures that this comparison is made over a large enough sample size to reduce noise and increase statistical significance. Failure modes include premature flipping, incorrect model versions, or misalignment between simulated and real-world outcomes.
